592.d: To make a logical distinction, make an invidious distinction. From apo and a compound of Alexandros and horizo; to disjoin.

679.d: Without stumbling or falling, sure-footed. Not stumbling, i.e. without sin.

1.d: The first letter of the alphabet.

493.d: Antipas, a Christian martyr of Pergamum. Contracted for a compound of anti and a derivative of pater; Antipas, a Christian.

904.d: Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab. Of Hebrew origin; Balak, a Moabite.

894.d: Wormwood. Of uncertain derivation; wormwood (figuratively) calamity).

3.d: Abaddon, Destroyer (i.e. Destroying Angel) or place of destruction (personified). Of Hebrew origin; a destroying angel.

623.d: Apollyon, The Destroying One, a Greek translation of the Hebrew: Abaddon. Active participle of apollumi; a destroyer.

974.d: A little papyrus roll. A diminutive of biblion; a booklet.

715.d: A bear. Probably from arkeo; a bear.

187.d: To reach maturity, become ripe, am in full vigor. From the same as akmen; to make a point, i.e. mature.

944.d: A frog. Of uncertain derivation; a frog.

717.d: Armageddon. Of Hebrew origin; Armageddon, a symbolic name.

239.d: Hallelujah, Praise the Lord. Of Hebrew origin; praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation.

969.d: A beryl, a precious stone of various colors, the best known being sea-green. Of uncertain derivation; a |beryl|.
